correctness.rationale: Convexity reduces each fixed-radius numerator to sign vertices. Exhausting the one-, two-, and three-projective-class cases gives bounds 1, 2, and at most (3+sqrt(3))/2, respectively. The last bound has an exact nonnegative-square certificate and is attained at radii sqrt(3)-1:1:1. With all radii one, the projective-sign count gives the sharp modified numerator 28 and value 7/3. The companion standard-library verifier checks all 64 sign-row triples and exact Q(sqrt(3)) witness identities.

value.rationale: This is the first cube dimension below the source’s m>=4 maximality threshold for the third-order constant. The exact pair of values resolves that natural finite-dimensional gap and shows quantitatively that allowing unequal radii strictly increases the third-order von Neumann–Jordan constant, with a closed algebraic optimizer. The result is therefore a structural boundary fact rather than a routine parameter substitution.
